title: Structured Data with JSON-LD
summary: Describe page entities in a machine-readable format for services such as search engines.

subtopics.title: Describe a page with JSON-LD
subtopics.explanation: JSON-LD is structured information written as a JSON script in the page. It can describe things such as an article, product, or event in a format search engines can interpret. The markup describes visible page content; it does not guarantee that a search result will show an enhancement.

subtopics.title: Choose an accurate schema type
subtopics.explanation: Choose the schema type that best matches what the page actually contains. An event page can describe its date and venue, while a product page can describe its offer. Do not add fields or ratings that users cannot find on the page; structured data must reflect the real content.

subtopics.title: Match the visible page
subtopics.explanation: Keep structured values consistent with the content people can read. If a page changes its price or date, update the structured data too. A mismatch can mislead search tools and users, and may make the markup ineligible for enhanced search presentation.

subtopics.title: Validate syntax and properties
subtopics.explanation: Validate the JSON syntax and the fields required by the chosen schema type. A trailing comma can break the script, while a missing property can make the description incomplete. Recheck after publishing because templates and content updates can change the generated markup.

subtopics.title: Understand search-result eligibility
subtopics.explanation: Valid structured data helps search engines understand a page, but it does not promise a rich result. Search systems decide whether an enhancement is useful and eligible. Keep the page valuable without special search treatment, and measure results instead of treating markup as a ranking shortcut.

foundations.overview: Structured data adds information about entities such as an article, product, or event. JSON-LD places that description in a script block. It should accurately match visible page content; it does not guarantee a special search result.
foundations.mentalModel: It is like adding a catalog card beside an object so others can identify it.
foundations.whyItMatters: Clear machine-readable descriptions can help services interpret a page.

keyTakeaways: JSON-LD is a JSON format for linked data.
Choose a schema type that matches the page.
Keep descriptions consistent with visible content.
Search engines decide whether to show enhanced results.
